title: COVID-19 remote work removes the need to commute
description: Working from home during the COVID-19 pandemic removed the need for regular bike commuting. Visible in the activity data as a complete gap in rides from April through June 2020 -- the only gap of its kind in the full 11-year history.

title: Chronic low back pain develops, initially misdiagnosed
description: Developed low back pain that prevented completing long hours on the bike. Shifted to a strictly-commuting riding regimen (short, low-intensity rides) specifically to minimize pain, replacing the long training and charity rides that had been the norm through 2019. Initially diagnosed as a bulging disk pressing on the sciatic nerve; physical therapy and steroid injections targeting that diagnosis did not provide relief. This is a separate, distinct cause from the COVID commuting gap (see covid-wfh-commute-gap), though both begin around the same time.

title: Diagnosis revised to spinal stenosis
description: Saw a new spine doctor who changed the diagnosis from a bulging disk/sciatic nerve compression to spinal stenosis causing inflammation of a specific nerve root.

title: Targeted steroid injection resolves back pain
description: Received a steroid injection targeting the specific nerve root identified in the May 2026 stenosis diagnosis. Resulted in complete relief from back pain for the first time in years. Confirmed in the activity data as a real inflection point: Peloton cardio resumed 24 days later (June 28) and a structured strength program began about a month later (July 5) -- both are the first of their kind in years/ever in this dataset.

title: New routine: commuting, strength training, and short intense Peloton cardio
description: Following pain relief, began a new three-part training routine: continued bike commuting (unchanged in distance/frequency), added structured strength training (first appears in the Strava export July 2026, as a trainer-led 'Week N Day N' program -- the only strength training logged anywhere in 11 years of data), and short, intense Peloton cardio sessions (HIIT/Tabata classes resumed June 28, 2026) in place of the longer, lower-intensity rides from the pre-injury era.

title: Trainer-led sessions logged after the fact -- raw duration is meaningless
description: Some strength sessions (named 'Trainer Session N' / 'Training Session N' in activities.csv, e.g. Jul 19, Jul 26, Aug 2) are live 1-hour appointments with a trainer that get logged into Hevy after the fact rather than tracked in real time. Their recorded elapsed_time (7-10 min) reflects how long the after-the-fact data entry took, not the session itself -- unlike the numbered 'Week N Day N' sessions, which are self-directed and tracked live. Treat the real duration of any 'Trainer/Training Session' entry as approximately 60 minutes (50 min training + 2x5 min stretching), not the logged value. Routine on a trainer-session day: a 15-20 min Peloton ride at home (typically Low Impact), then walk to the trainer's house (four houses away), the session itself (trainer records everything on paper), walk home, then log the session in Hevy from a photo of the paper notes -- often after showering and eating, so the logged timestamp can trail the real session by an hour or more. Every trainer-led session in this dataset except the very first ('Training Assessment', which predates this export) has a same-day Peloton ride beforehand that served as that warm-up. Because of the logging delay, matching a session to its warm-up ride requires comparing calendar dates, not a tight end-to-start time gap -- a gap check works for the self-directed 'Week N Day N' sessions (logged live) but not these.
